Record date: 2129-09-12
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 09/12/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Continued shortness of breath, persistent cough, and reduced lower extremity swelling.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up after a 3-day hospitalization for exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and congestive heart failure (CHF). During his hospital stay, he received intravenous furosemide for fluid overload, systemic corticosteroids for airway inflammation, and antibiotics for pneumonia. The patient reports significant improvement in his respiratory symptoms since discharge, noting that his shortness of breath has decreased markedly, and he is now able to ambulate with minimal assistance. The productive cough persists but is less frequent, with sputum production reduced in volume and now clear.
He continues to experience some fatigue but states that he is sleeping better due to the trazodone, with fewer nocturnal awakenings. Mr. Fairfax reports that the bilateral lower extremity swelling has improved considerably, with less tenderness and pitting noted.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + fatigue, - weight gain, - fever, - chills, - night sweats. Pulmonary - + improved shortness of breath, + decreased productive cough, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain, + orthopnea resolved, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + mild joint pain, - worsening bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 138/82 mmHg - Heart Rate: 82 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 22 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 92% on room air.
General: The patient appears well-nourished, alert, and in no acute distress.
HEENT: No nasal flaring; oropharynx clear, no signs of dehydration.
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, with mild wheezing noted on forced expiration; no crackles present.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops; peripheral pulses intact and symmetric.
Extremities: Mild bilateral lower extremity edema, with minimal pitting; tenderness on palpation has resolved.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) stable post-exacerbation; improved respiratory status with resolution of pneumonia. 2. Congestive heart failure improving with effective diuresis and management strategies; ongoing monitoring required. 3. Insomnia improving with trazodone; continued evaluation of sleep quality necessary.
PLAN
1. Discontinue intravenous furosemide; transition to oral furosemide 40 mg daily for ongoing management of fluid status. 2. Continue systemic corticosteroids (prednisone 40 mg daily) for an additional 5 days, then taper to 20 mg daily. 3. Maintain azithromycin therapy for a total of 5 days; monitor for any signs of infection recurrence. 4. Reinforce the use of nebulized treatments with albuterol and budesonide every 4 hours as needed, and continue ipratropium bromide. 5. Schedule a follow-up appointment in one week to reassess respiratory function and CHF status. 6. Educate Mr. Fairfax on daily weight monitoring and adherence to medication regimen; emphasize the importance of reporting any recurrence of symptoms. 7. Consider referral to pulmonary rehabilitation to enhance functional capacity and improve quality of life.
Mr. Fairfax demonstrated understanding of the treatment plan and expressed willingness to comply with follow-up recommendations.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax was discharged home with a comprehensive discharge plan and follow-up instructions. He was instructed to seek immediate medical attention if he experiences any worsening of symptoms or new concerns arise.
